body_markdown:
*A second Siemens Energy F-class natural gas turbine and two generators arrive at Project Matador, demonstrating Fermi’s advantage as global demand pushes power generation equipment lead times years into the future.*


As AI accelerates, one of the industry’s biggest constraints isn’t computing, land or capital. It’s access to power.


Across the industry, demand for large-scale power generation equipment has surged, with manufacturing lead times for new natural gas turbines now extending into the early and mid-2030s. For developers racing to build AI infrastructure, securing the equipment needed to generate electricity has become one of the industry’s biggest challenges.


At Fermi, that challenge is our competitive advantage.


Project Matador has reached another milestone with the arrival of its second Siemens Energy SGT6-5000F turbine at the company’s energy and AI campus near Amarillo, Texas, alongside two corresponding generators.


The equipment joins the first Siemens F-class turbine, which arrived in September, bringing the total to two Siemens F-class turbines and their corresponding generators on-site, alongside Fermi’s growing inventory of power generation assets.


### **From Factory Queues to Equipment on the Ground**


The global race to build AI data centers has created unprecedented demand for reliable, large-scale electricity. But the equipment required to generate that power cannot be manufactured overnight.


As developers compete for limited manufacturing capacity, access to generation equipment has become a defining factor in how quickly new data center projects can move forward.


Fermi has taken a different approach.


Rather than developing data centers first and securing power later, Fermi is building both the power generation infrastructure and the data centers together at Project Matador.


By securing generation equipment ahead of growing industry demand, Fermi is positioned to advance its development timeline while others face extended manufacturing queues.


### **Building the Backbone for AI**


Project Matador is being developed as a large-scale, privately powered energy and AI campus in the Texas Panhandle, where Fermi is building both the power generation infrastructure and the data centers it will serve. By developing both on a single campus, Fermi is creating an integrated solution designed to meet the enormous energy demands of artificial intelligence without placing additional demand on the public electric grid.


The Siemens SGT6-5000F turbines are part of a growing portfolio of power generation equipment Fermi has secured to support this development.


Their arrival represents more than another delivery. It demonstrates how Fermi’s strategy of developing power generation and data center infrastructure together is becoming a physical reality at Project Matador.


As the AI industry continues searching for power, Fermi is building both sides of the equation.


**The AI industry is waiting for power. Fermi is taking delivery.**


Fermi is where AI gets power.
